precepts.text: Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? To his own master he standeth or falleth. Our real master is Christ.
precepts.point: Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal. They claimed they were the masters; did they do that? No. They lived in the big house while we lived in the outhouse, and we never got the forty acres and the mule. So they showed themselves hypocrites and impostors. The verse ends: knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
When we read precept upon precept, in the context of the scriptures, we see how we have been lied to as a people. Paul asks: “Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth.”

Who are you to judge another man’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. So our real master is Christ. That is the “Master in heaven” of Colossians 4:1, the one both servants and masters answer to.

And the servant is not left alone: “Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.” There it is. For God is able to make him stand.

precepts.text: Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? The master is Christ. One man esteemeth one day above another: the Jews that followed Moses esteemed the day through sacrifice. Another esteemeth every day alike: the Israelites that followed Christ were not doing the sacrifices; they accepted what Christ did. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind: fully persuaded that Christ's sacrifice absolves you of sin. There was a dispensation of time from the crucifixion until the temple fell where people were still struggling to accept that; it is not talking about being fully persuaded on whether to keep God's laws. He that regardeth the day through sacrifice regardeth it unto the Lord, and he that regardeth not the day, because he accepted Christ, to the Lord he doth not regard it. For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord.
precepts.point: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holy day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days. The meat is the meat offerings and the drink is the drink offerings; do not let a Christian use this verse to say it is talking about eating pork or getting drunk. This is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said.
precepts.why:
Here is another precept about them judging people: “Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.” Remember who the master is: the master is Christ.

“One man esteemeth one day above another”. How did they esteem it? Through sacrifice: on the sabbath day you had to offer two lambs of the first year. The Jews that were following Moses esteemed one day above another through sacrifice. “another esteemeth every day alike”: the Israelites that followed Christ were not doing the sacrifices. They said, we are just going to accept what Christ did; we are not doing burnt offerings. Like today: here is the sabbath day, and we are not esteeming it with animal sacrifice.

“Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.” Fully persuaded in Christ: that his sacrifice, his dying for you, forgives your sins. There was a dispensation of time from the time he was crucified until the temple fell, when people went back to the temple and were still struggling to accept that Christ coming to die would absolve them of sin, and they were given time to be fully persuaded. It is not being fully persuaded about keeping the laws of God, like adultery. No.

“He that regardeth the day, regardeth it unto the Lord”: regarding it through sacrifice. “and he that regardeth not the day, to the Lord he doth not regard it”, because he accepted Christ and did not need the goats and the bulls. “He that eateth, eateth to the Lord”: eating the animal sacrifice, you eat to the Lord and give God thanks, and he that eats not gives God thanks as well. “For none of us liveth to himself, and no man dieth to himself.” “For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord’s.”

precepts.text: And he that doubteth is damned if he eat, because he eateth not of faith: for whatsoever is not of faith is sin. Some ate of the sacrifices but were not fully persuaded at this point.
precepts.point: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holy day, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days. The meat is the meat offerings and the drink is the drink offerings; do not let a Christian use this verse to say it is talking about eating pork or getting drunk. This is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said.
precepts.why:
“And he that doubteth is damned if he eat, because he eateth not of faith: for whatsoever is not of faith is sin.”

There were some who doubted that Christ’s blood was able to absolve them of their sins, and they ate of the sacrifices. Some ate, but they were not fully persuaded at this point. That is the doubt Paul is talking about.

People say fully persuaded means, I am not fully clear that eating pork is wrong, because of the New Testament. That is not what it is talking about. It is being persuaded that Christ’s blood would absolve them from sin. So the eating in Romans 14, like the meat of Colossians 2:16, is the eating of the sacrifices, not the eating of unclean meat.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come

precepts.why: “Him that is weak in the faith receive ye”: some brothers have weaker faith than others, so you deal with them at first. “But not to doubtful disputations”: there’s a limit to that. Disputation means they want to argue with you; show them the door.

points: Whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord's. This is the mindset we have to have. Do not let fear of things mess with your spirit. We have to build ourselves up to where we are not afraid of being with the Lord.
